targetText: "No one can discredit revolutionary Social-Democracy as long as it does not discredit itself." That maxim always comes to mind, and must always be borne in mind, when any major theoretical or tactical proposition of Marxism is victorious, or even placed on the order of the day, and when, besides outright and resolute opponents, it is assailed by friends who hopelessly discredit and disparage it and turn it into a caricature.
summary: Lenin warns that revolutionary Marxism is often damaged most not by class enemies, but by dogmatic allies who turn nuanced dialectical theory into rigid, absurd caricatures.

targetText: "Defence of the fatherland" in a war waged by an oppressed nation against a foreign oppressor is not a deception. Socialists are not opposed to "defence of the fatherland" in such a war.
summary: Lenin clarifies the dialectical Marxist distinction regarding national defense: while slogans of defending the fatherland in an imperialist war between colonizing powers are chauvinist fraud, defending an oppressed nation against imperialist invasion is legitimate and progressive.

targetText: National self-determination is the same as the struggle for complete national liberation, for complete independence, against annexation, and socialists cannot: without ceasing to be socialists: reject such a struggle in whatever form, right down to an uprising or war.
summary: Lenin asserts that advocating national self-determination means actively supporting the right of subjugated peoples to complete sovereignty, including armed national liberation struggle against foreign domination.
